The path

An incident doesn't end when the trucks leave.

Most behavioral health support arrives late and leaves early. We're structured around the full arc — from the planning cycle before an activation through the years of recovery after it.

Phase 01 · Blue sky

Readiness

Pre-incident training and planning so your people already know the playbook when the activation comes.

Phase 02 · 0–72 hrs

Deployment

Rapid needs assessment and on-site stabilization at shelters, EOCs, and staging areas.

Phase 03 · Weeks 1–6

Sustainment

Reset support for crews working extended operational periods. Where retention is won or lost.

Phase 04 · Long recovery

Capacity

Building internal strength so the community and its agencies carry themselves forward without us.

    The catalog

    Start with one course. Or work the whole path.

    Every course is built from real deployments — not a lecture recorded off a slide deck. Lessons run six to fourteen minutes so they fit between shifts.

    How the training runs

    Four stages, in this order, on purpose.

    You can't practice skills you haven't learned, and you can't sustain work you were never prepared for. The sequence is the method.

    STAGE 01

    Learn

    Short video and written modules you can finish between shifts. No eight-hour webinar.

    STAGE 02

    Practice

    Scenario walkthroughs drawn from real deployments, with the wrong answers shown too.

    STAGE 03

    Apply

    Live cohort sessions with a Capacity Path trainer. Bring your own hard call.

    STAGE 04

    Sustain

    Refreshers, team debrief tools, and somewhere to come back after a bad one.

    What gets taught

    The biology, not the buzzwords.

    Window of tolerance. Hyperarousal and shutdown. The phases of disaster and where communities actually fall apart. Where emotion registers in the body and what that means for someone standing in front of you at a shelter.

    This is the same material Capacity Path teaches to county leadership on deployment, built into courses your whole workforce can take on a phone.

    The portal

    Assign it. Track it. Prove it.

    Administrators assign courses to a whole department with a due date, and see completion as it comes in. When an audit asks who was trained and when, the answer is one export away.

    About

    Built for how people actually function in unstable environments.

    Capacity Path exists because the behavioral health load after a disaster lands on agencies that were never resourced to carry it — and because most of the help that arrives is designed for a clinic, not a staging area.

    The modality

    Community Crisis Stabilization

    Our signature modality is built on a simple premise: people in crisis are not empty. They arrive with resilience and strengths already in them, and the fastest route to stability is reaching for that rather than replacing it.

    We work to embed Community Crisis Stabilization directly into public safety and public health infrastructure — not as an outside service that shows up and leaves, but as a capability those systems hold themselves.

    C.O.P.E.S. framework detail to be added

    Why it works

    The people who do this well are not the warmest ones. They're the ones who can stand still in a bad room and not need to fill the silence. That is trainable, and training it is the whole point.

    Where we've worked

    Nineteen-plus nationally declared disasters.

    Hurricanes, wildfire, volcanic activity, and pandemic response across Florida, the Caribbean, and the Pacific — alongside county emergency management, health systems, school districts, and volunteer organizations.
